newsitem.title: FRANCE: BNP head declines comment on CIC.
newsitem.headline: BNP head declines comment on CIC.

text.p: Banque Nationale de Paris chairman Michel Pebereau on Monday declined to comment on a report in daily Le Monde that his bank was making an offer for CIC, a large regional banking group that is being privatised.
A finance ministry tender for offers expired at 1600 GMT on Monday.
Pebereau, questioned at a news conference, simply reiterated that the terms and conditions of the tender did not allow candidates to reveal their intentions.
But Savings bank group Caisse d'Epargne said it would not make an offer for Credit Commercial et Industriel (CIC).
The government has asked for offers within the trade for 67 percent of CIC, which is controlled by state insurer GAN.
Juergen Sarrazin, head BNP partner Dresdner Bank, said at the same news conference, that he had no comment.
Le Monde said BNP would make an offer without Dresdner's involvement, but it had the consent of its German partner.
